doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: Starting on saxophone in 1919 and the C melody question
summary: Paul began on E-flat alto in 1919; they discuss why C melody was never used in New Orleans bands.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I'll say, I started playing music in 1919. September, I'll never forget the gate. September the 3rd. The saxophone, just one month. Well, we formed a little band, Lawrence Murad and so forth.
That's to get back to that, that was the E-flat alto.
I was going to ask once, somebody told me most of the fellas started with the C melody. Remember those old days when everybody used the C melody, I thought, but you didn't get in on that.

No, in fact, no one used the C melody around New Orleans. I don't know any otherwise, because they always figured that a C melody was too soft for a band. And so orchestration was put up though, with the music for C melody, but we never did use it.
I know a lot of people bought those and they wouldn't even have a part for them in late years anymore.
